Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: No evidence of CRVS integration with a national data exchange. Guinea's civil registration system faces challenges; November 2025 workshop focused on health information system interoperability (not civil registration). World Bank DE4A 2021 noted CRVS was not integrated with foundational ID.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) is superseded by direct evidence from Guinea's official PN-RAVEC civil registration programme website (fetched in full), which states as an explicit objective that the interoperable Personal Identification Number (NPI) issued to each registered citizen is intended to enable communication with the Electoral Register and other national registries. A World Bank-funded ANDE workshop on 'e-Services and interoperability of public systems' (launched April 2026, page fetched in full) is separately working on ID-document services and cross-system interoperability. Neither source shows this as operational yet — both describe stated objectives or an ongoing workshop, not a live data link. Recalculated to 2 (Planned) rather than 0 (Unknown). This rests on an interpretive step (reading RAVEC's stated objectives as evidence of planning specifically for CRVS-to-exchange integration) and is flagged for human review to confirm the inference is sound.
revised_comments: Guinea's national civil registration programme (PN-RAVEC) is built around an interoperable Personal Identification Number (NPI) intended to link civil-status records with other national registries, but this interoperability is not yet operational. A World Bank-supported workshop on e-services and public-system interoperability, convened by the state digitalisation agency ANDE in April 2026, is working towards this goal alongside identity-document services. CRVS integration into a functioning data exchange therefore remains at the planning stage.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: No evidence found of tax/revenue system integration with a national data exchange platform. TELEMO addresses public procurement transparency but no documented API-level integration between tax authority and other government registries.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Guinea has well-developed sector-specific revenue platforms — the tax authority's e-Tax system and the Guichet Unique du Commerce Extérieur (GUCEG), interconnected with commercial banks, the central bank, customs and the port authority, reporting over 84% national deployment and securing roughly 18,000 billion Guinean francs of customs revenue in 2025 (per a June 2026 relaunch event, fetched in full) — plus an August 2025 customs-cargo tracking interconnection agreement. However, a November 2025 CSEA Africa policy brief (fetched in full) explicitly characterises these as siloed platforms built under separate donor/ministry initiatives without shared APIs or a central interoperability framework. Since the variable asks about integration 'into the exchange platform' (i.e. the cross-government data exchange), and no such central exchange yet exists, recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated) rather than upgraded, with the sector-level digitisation noted for context.
revised_comments: Guinea operates well-developed sector-specific digital revenue platforms, including the e-Tax system for domestic taxation and the Guichet Unique du Commerce Extérieur (GUCEG), which is interconnected with commercial banks, the central bank, customs and the port authority and reports over 84% national deployment. These systems, however, remain siloed and were developed independently of one another and of any cross-government data exchange, without shared APIs or a common interoperability framework. Tax and revenue data is therefore not yet integrated into a unified government data exchange platform.

revision_notes: A November 2025 CSEA Africa policy brief (fetched in full) confirms Guinea has no unified, interoperable government data exchange platform at all, and no evidence of AI use for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics within such a system was found in any source. Since there is now positive evidence that no cross-government data exchange exists to host AI capabilities, recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (No) rather than leaving it Unknown.
revised_comments: No evidence of artificial intelligence being used for data quality assurance, fraud detection or predictive analytics within a government data exchange context. Guinea does not yet operate a unified, interoperable government data exchange platform into which such AI capabilities could be embedded; current digitalisation efforts, such as the FUGAS civil-service registry and TELEMO e-procurement platform, are administrative digitisation tools rather than analytics platforms.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: TELEMO explicitly designed to improve governance transparency and fight corruption in public procurement. The Minister presented detailed sector review for 2025 with quantified results. However, no public dashboard for data exchange operations; data protection law is still under adoption. Limited public reporting on data exchange specifically.

Both originally cited sources were re-fetched and support general digital-sector transparency but not data-exchange-specific reporting, as the original comment already noted. Additional evidence: the state digitalisation agency ANDE publishes its interoperability rules and standards framework (Règles d'Interopérabilité des SI) publicly on its website, which is a relevant but modest transparency signal for data-exchange governance specifically. No public dashboard or dedicated data-sharing-agreement disclosure exists. Value Name label differs cosmetically from the metadata scale wording ('Low - Limited Disclosure' vs '2=Low = Limited Disclosure') but the code is unaffected.
revised_comments: Guinea's state digitalisation agency (ANDE) publishes its interoperability rules and standards framework online, and the government provides periodic public reporting on digital-sector progress, including a detailed 2025 sector review presented by the Minister of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy. However, no public dashboard or dedicated reporting exists on data exchange operations, governance or inter-agency data-sharing agreements specifically, and national data protection legislation remains under adoption. Transparency is therefore best characterised as limited disclosure rather than comprehensive public reporting.
